status: Per-obligation status as of this release. 24 proved and discharged by `bend PROOF.bend` (and re-checked by the Lean-proved BendTT kernel under `--verdict`); 3 proved in part, with the proved half in LAWS.bend and the remaining half recorded in LAWS.pending.bend as prose, since none of the three is a statement about this tree's algebra; 5 not applicable until the milestone named in `reason`. LAWS.pending.bend holds no open law. TRUST.md is the boundary this table summarises.

laws.name: Identity mapping
laws.statement: identify is injective; lookup round-trips within one universe.
laws.proof_symbol: Uni.intern_round_trip (proofs/intern.bend); Uni.inj (proofs/interninj.bend), on Trie.get_put_other and Trie.get_same_path (proofs/trieput.bend)
laws.backed_by: by construction in adapters/git/intern.bend: one ordinal per distinct complete key, compared on the complete key.
laws.proved_part: Both halves. The round trip: interning an object id and then looking it up in the table interning returned gives the ordinal interning returned, for any universe and any id, with no well-formedness hypothesis. And injectivity: over a universe built by interning a list (Uni.of_list, which is what the importer does), two ids that share an ordinal are the same id. The induction carries a decidable bound -- every ordinal in the table is below the counter -- so the hypothesis is data and can be used as often as the argument needs, which a pointwise one could not be under the affine discipline. Reading back the one write is settled by casing on whether two keys descend the trie the same way (Trie.path_ne), not on whether the keys are equal: key injectivity is never needed.
laws.gap: None, under the stated hypothesis. Injectivity needs Uni.room(os, f): that the U32 counter strictly grew at every step of the run. That is not decoration -- intern hands out next and then increments it as a machine word, so a wrapped counter really would give two different objects the same ordinal. A source of fewer than 2^32 objects satisfies it.

laws.name: Generation lifting
laws.statement: Append-only lifting preserves membership of old identities and union/intersection/difference; new members are absent.
laws.unlocks: Reuse old set roots after universe growth
laws.reason: M2. No stored generations to lift between.

laws.name: Pointwise set operations
laws.statement: Member(union/intersection/difference(A,B),x) equals the Boolean specification.

laws.name: Representation refinement
laws.statement: Set difference, union and intersection are pointwise at the production depth, for structurally valid operands and every U32 ordinal.
laws.backed_by: the differential in tests.bend and tools/differential.sh: the production traversal uses these operations throughout.
laws.refuted_as_first_stated: The original statements had no hypotheses and were false. At a leaf, PFull means that leaf's own 4096 ordinals while the tile it converts to reads False past 4096; above a leaf, a sparse or dense payload is a shape PSet.valid rejects and the node operations read it as empty while PSet.mem reads it as a member. Both counterexamples run in tests.bend.
laws.proved_part: All three, at depth 20 -- which covers 2^32 ordinals, so no hypothesis about the ordinal survives. Structural validity is the only hypothesis, and it is what every stored generation is checked against on load.

laws.name: Representation conversion
laws.statement: Compressing a full-width tile preserves membership for every ordinal the leaf covers. (Restated with those two conditions; both have counterexamples without them.)
laws.backed_by: tests.bend: the sparse/dense crossover at 64 and 65 members preserves membership and size.
laws.refuted_as_first_stated: The original statements had no hypotheses and were false. At a leaf, PFull means that leaf's own 4096 ordinals while the tile it converts to reads False past 4096; above a leaf, a sparse or dense payload is a shape PSet.valid rejects and the node operations read it as empty while PSet.mem reads it as a member. Both counterexamples run in tests.bend.
laws.proved_part: Compression changes no member, whichever of the four representations it picks, for a 128-word tile and an ordinal the leaf covers. Zero bits means PZero and no member, by counting; a full 4096 means PFull and every member, by the pigeonhole; the dense arm is the identity; the sparse arm enumerates, and the enumeration lists what the walk holds, which is what the address holds.

laws.name: Boolean rewrites
laws.statement: Each admitted Boolean rewrite preserves membership in one universe.
laws.backed_by: tests.bend: the SPEC 4.1 counterexamples fail the build if a forbidden rewrite is ever added.
laws.proved_part: The emptiness test only answers True for a set with no members -- which is what the admitted rewrites rest on, since it is an early exit that stops at the first word with a bit in it rather than counting -- and the three rewrites are then instances of S-02 with an empty operand.

laws.name: Persistent updates
laws.statement: Returned updated root has patch semantics; every retained old root has unchanged denotation.
laws.proof_symbol: PSet.mem_insert (proofs/leaf.bend), PSet.insert_keeps and PSet.from_list_contains (proofs/insert.bend), PSet.insert_only and PSet.from_list_only (proofs/only.bend)
laws.reason: M2. No persistent derived store in this release: pp imports per invocation.
laws.backed_by: Bend's affine values for the sharing half.
laws.note: Was recorded as not applicable while there was no persistent set. core/set.bend has had PSet.insert since M1, so the obligation is live.
laws.proved_part: Inserting an ordinal into a well-shaped set leaves it present; inserting never loses a member that was already there; and inserting adds nothing else. Together that pins PSet.insert down at every ordinal, and a set folded up from a list has exactly the ordinals on that list. The sharing half -- that retained old roots are undisturbed -- is a property of Bend affine values, not an equation; TRUST.md section 3.
laws.gap: The sharing half: that every retained old root still denotes what it did. That is a property of Bend's affine values -- a persistent update copies the path it changes and cannot reach the nodes it did not copy -- and not an equation over any symbol that can observe it.
laws.refuted_as_first_stated: The original statement had no hypothesis and was false: a PDense leaf narrower than 128 words loses the bit it was just given, because Words.set past the end of a tile changes nothing. tests.bend runs that counterexample permanently.

laws.name: Least fixed point
laws.statement: C(R) is the least edge-closed set containing R.
laws.backed_by: spec/closure.bend is the definition operationally; the fixed point is reached within the universe size by construction of the fuel.
laws.proved_part: All three things "least fixed point" says. C(R) contains R. C(R) is edge-closed -- by a pigeonhole over the rounds: a round that is not edge-closed exhibits a witness through the fused difference list and so is strictly bigger than the one before, every set is inside a bounding set the graph respects, and that bounds how many rounds can change. And leastness: C(R) is inside every edge-closed set containing R, by induction over the rounds carrying PSet.is_subset, which is decidable data rather than a quantified hypothesis.
laws.gap: None. The fuel hypothesis is that the number of rounds exceeds the bounding set's cardinality, which is what the production fuel is derived from.

laws.name: Traversal refinement
laws.statement: Production frontier traversal returns C(R) and terminates on admitted finite graphs.
laws.backed_by: the closure certificate (C-04) per query, plus the five-graph differential against the specification closure in tests.bend, plus tools/differential.sh against `git rev-list --objects`.
laws.proved_part: The frontier traversal returns exactly the specification closure. The traversal never leaves the closure, because every vertex it adds is one edge from something it had already accepted and the closure is edge-closed; and the closure never leaves the traversal, because a finished traversal is itself edge-closed and holds the roots, so leastness (C-01) puts the closure inside it. What makes a finished traversal edge-closed is a decidable invariant on the frontier -- Reach.settled -- carried across every level rotation.

laws.name: Closure algebra
laws.statement: Closure is extensive, monotone, idempotent, empty-preserving and union-preserving.
laws.backed_by: tests.bend: union preservation, extensivity, idempotence and closure-of-empty on the counterexample graph.
laws.proved_part: All five. Empty preservation and extensivity were proved earlier. Monotonicity in the roots, union preservation and idempotence follow from C-01: each round is monotone and commutes with union because the successor image does, and idempotence is leastness applied to a set that is already edge-closed.

laws.name: Closure certificate soundness/completeness
laws.statement: The rank/predecessor and edge-closure checker accepts only exact closures; every finite exact closure admits such a certificate.
laws.unlocks: Checked cached or alternative closure proposals
laws.backed_by: closure/cert.bend Cert.check, run by `pp git verify`; soundness argued in closure/cert.bend and TRUST.md, not mechanised. tests.bend checks it accepts a real closure and rejects both a tampered-up and a tampered-down one.
laws.proved_part: Acceptance implies exactness, not just the four conditions separately. Conditions 1 and 2 make the candidate an edge-closed set containing the roots, so leastness (C-01) puts the closure inside it; condition 3's well-founded predecessor chains walk every member back to a root, which puts it inside the closure because the closure is edge-closed and each member is one edge from its predecessor.
laws.gap: Completeness -- that every finite exact closure admits such a certificate -- is not mechanised. It is the direction a checker does not need: the checker's job is to reject a wrong closure, and soundness is what rules that out.

laws.name: Checkpoint shortcut
laws.statement: Replacing exploration at a vertex by its validated cached closure preserves the full result.
laws.unlocks: Checkpoint indexes and shared ancestor reuse

laws.name: Least missing set
laws.statement: K subset H union T iff (K minus H) subset T, for K=C(R) and arbitrary H.

laws.name: Readiness
laws.statement: isReady(K,H) iff K subset H iff K minus H is empty.

laws.name: Missing composition
laws.statement: (A union B) minus H = (A minus H) union (B minus H); A minus (H1 union H2) = (A minus H1) minus H2.
laws.unlocks: Shared requirements and tiered inventory filtering

laws.name: Ordinal partition
laws.statement: Disjoint valid ordinal intervals cover the result exactly once; pointwise Boolean operations commute with restriction.
laws.public_law: LAWS.bend tile_*_is_pointwise, which are stated at a position and so commute with restriction to disjoint ranges

laws.name: Disjoint statistics
laws.statement: Stats(disjoint_union tiles)=fold(componentwise_add, Stats(tiles)).
laws.public_law: LAWS.bend statistics_have_a_left_identity, statistics_have_a_right_identity, statistics_add_commutatively, statistics_add_associatively, every_object_counts_once

laws.name: Validated query rewrites
laws.statement: For every admitted rewrite, denotation before equals denotation after; validation precedes elimination.
laws.backed_by: tests.bend counterexamples; the rewrites are instances of Boolean laws proved at the tile level.
laws.proved_part: The whole pass. Rw.simplify, recursion into Reach and Filter included, produces an expression with exactly the members of the one it replaced, at the production depth, for every ordinal. The induction carries PSet.same -- the decidable two-way subset -- rather than a pointwise equality, which under the affine discipline could not be used twice; closure, filtering and the three set operations are each proved to respect it.

laws.name: Fused difference statistics
laws.statement: FusedStats(A,B)=Stats(decode(A) minus decode(B)).

laws.name: Compiler soundness
laws.statement: observe(execute(compile(W,q)))=denote(q,W) for admitted total core inputs.
laws.proved_part: The evaluator computes the denotation: for a well-formed expression over a valid source, running the machine gives a set with exactly the members the specification evaluator's denotation has. The machine is a control word, a stack of frames and one tail call per step, because two non-tail self-calls in one def overrun this runtime's frame limit; the invariant relating its stack to the remaining denotation is decidable data (Ev.stack_ok), which is what lets the induction use it at every frame.

laws.name: Batch deduplication
laws.statement: Deduplicating equal requests/operand pairs and restoring caller positions preserves every result and order.
laws.reason: M3. No batch matrix command yet.
laws.backed_by: `pp git matrix` deduplicates identical inventories and answers one cell per distinct inventory, reporting `distinct_inventories` and naming the cell each duplicate shares with. tests.bend checks that three cells over two distinct inventories report `cells 3 distinct 2` with the third row pointing at the first.
laws.note: Was recorded as not applicable while there was no batch command. `pp git matrix` shipped in M4, so the obligation is live.
laws.stated_in: LAWS.bend (order and what a reused answer is) and LAWS.pending.bend (that it is the answer the cell would have computed)
laws.proved_part: The order half, in full: Cmd.matrix.rows builds the output with an accumulator and reverses once, and it agrees with the same walk written in order, with one row per cell -- so a cell position in the output is its position in the input whatever deduplication did to its answer. And what a reused answer is: the lookup agrees with a plain find-first-by-name, so a duplicate reuses the recorded answer of the first cell whose name it points at and nothing the deduplication invented.
laws.gap: That the reused answer is the answer the duplicate cell would have computed. Cmd.matrix.same compares two inventories with PSet.is_subset both ways, which now gives equal members; going from equal members to an equal statistic needs the enumeration to agree with membership, which is now proved and published as a_valid_set_lists_exactly_its_members, for any set that passed the store's own validity check. What remains is carrying that equality into the statistic: the members agree ordinal by ordinal, and an equality quantified over ordinals cannot be used twice under Bend's affine discipline, so the step to an equal fold needs the same decidable form the subset converse needs.

laws.name: Inventory maintenance
laws.statement: maintain(K,H,remove,add)=fresh(K,(H minus remove) union add).

laws.name: Graph extension
laws.statement: Under complete unchanged old outgoing adjacency, old-root closure is preserved by the identity embedding.

laws.name: Cache binding
laws.statement: A reused value is bound to exact universe/graph/policy/root/weight/input generations.

laws.name: Reachability witness
laws.statement: Returned explanation begins at a requested root, ends at the requested object, and every step is a policy edge.
laws.proof_symbol: Explain.path_steps, Explain.walk_ends_at_target, Explain.accepts_root_head, Explain.accepts_last, Explain.checked_edge, Explain.checked_rest, Explain.accepts_steps (proofs/witness.bend); Ex.path_root (proofs/layering.bend), Lv.closure_chain and Lv.witness_root (proofs/levels.bend)
laws.backed_by: closure/explain.bend Explain.valid checks all three parts on every witness `pp git explain` emits, not trusting the producer; tests.bend checks it rejects a path that skips an edge and one that starts off-root.
laws.proved_part: All three parts, twice over. Of a returned witness -- pp git explain runs Explain.valid and exits non-zero when it fails -- all three, with the step fold unfolded into a per-step law so "every step is a policy edge" follows by walking the list rather than by trusting the checker. And of a produced one: two with no hypothesis at all, and the third, that it starts at a requested root, from the traversal's levels being a genuine breadth-first layering, which is now proved of Reach.closure rather than assumed.
laws.note: The check is kept and still gates the exit. A cached or heuristically produced witness is not this producer's, and SPEC 4.4's stance is that a witness is accepted on its own terms.
laws.gap: None. The producer-side law has one hypothesis: that the target appears in some level, which is what "the object is reachable" means and what "a witness was produced at all" means. Explain.path answers the empty list for an object no level holds, and the empty list starts nowhere, so the law is false without it rather than merely unproved.

laws.name: Word refinement
laws.statement: U32 difference/popcount and final-word masking implement bounded bit membership/count.
laws.production_symbol: core/word.bend U32.diff / U32.popcount / U32.mask, core/words.bend U32.test
laws.public_law: LAWS.bend word_difference_is_pointwise, word_intersection_is_pointwise, word_union_is_pointwise, shifting_right_reads_the_next_bit_up, the_tail_mask_hides_every_padding_bit, popcount_counts_the_bits_that_are_set, the_fast_bit_test_agrees_with_the_bit_vector

laws.name: Checked numeric refinement
laws.statement: Limb conversion/addition/comparison agree with Naturals in range; overflow is detected.

laws.name: Plan execution refinement
laws.statement: Every leaf/reduction executes its specified result with bounded reads and exclusive output writes under documented backend contracts.
laws.reason: M4. No Metal leaf-job plan dispatched by `auto` yet.

laws.name: Serialization
laws.statement: decode(encode(valid_value)) preserves denotation; accepted untrusted data satisfies structural invariants.
laws.reason: M2. No decoder yet; core/set.bend PSet.valid is the structural check it will be stated over.
laws.backed_by: index/store.bend validates a decoded generation structurally on load -- magic, declared format, declared object count against the objects actually present, hex width, and every successor index in range -- and rejects with CorruptIndex rather than answering. SPEC 6.5 requires that and says a checksum is not a substitute. tools/differential.sh corrupts a stored generation four ways and checks each is rejected, deriving each corruption from the file so it cannot silently become a no-op.
laws.note: Was recorded as not applicable while there was no derived store. M2 shipped one, so the obligation is live.
laws.proved_part: What structural validity rules out -- at any depth above a leaf a valid set is PZero, PFull or a branch, never a payload -- and what accepting a decode means: an accepted store declared exactly as many objects as the file holds, and a rejected one always reports a stable error class rather than failing silently. Those are the two ways a loader can be quietly wrong.
laws.gap: That decode inverts encode. It is a round trip through text -- the encoder renders numbers and hex digests into a line format and the decoder parses them back -- so it needs the show/parse round trip for Nat, U32 and object ids before anything about generations can be said. The differential checks the round trip observationally instead: a stored generation answers identically to the import that produced it, on both policies, and four kinds of corruption are rejected, each derived from the file so it cannot silently become a no-op.

laws.name: Metadata parser
laws.statement: Parsing is sound and complete within declared metadata grammar and explicit size limits.
laws.stated_in: LAWS.bend (the parser never reads short) and LAWS.pending.bend (the grammar)
laws.backed_by: tools/differential.sh over a corpus with a merge, a tag to a tag, a tag to a tree, a tag to a blob, a symlink, a zero-byte blob, a non-UTF-8 tree entry name and a gitlink.
laws.gap: Soundness and completeness for the declared grammar as a whole. The grammar it has to be complete for is Git own, so what would make it a law is a grammar predicate written in Bend and faithful to Git rather than read off the parser; one read off the parser would make the law true by construction and worth nothing. The differential corpus is what stands in for it.
laws.proved_part: The two parts that are statements about the parser alone rather than about agreeing with Git: an object id is read at exactly the format width, so a short one is an invalid id and not a silently truncated one; and a body is taken by its declared length, so a record whose length overruns the buffer is rejected and not read short. Those are the failure modes that matter -- a short id is a different id, and would intern as a new object.

laws.name: Git policies
laws.statement: Parsed Git objects map to exactly the specified full/tree-data internal edges and external references.
laws.backed_by: tools/differential.sh checks the tree-data policy against `rev-parse` plus `ls-tree -r -t` on three repositories, with gitlink entries excluded, over a corpus with a merge, a tag chain, a symlink, a zero-byte blob, a non-UTF-8 tree entry name and a gitlink.
laws.proved_part: Both halves. At a row: an ordinal survives Idx.filter_succ exactly when it was in the successor row and is not itself a commit. At an edge: the same statement about Graph.edge over the two adjacency tables Idx.assemble.tries stores, given that the metadata table describes the source vertex -- which the importer guarantees and Graph.domain_ok checks. The lift goes through proofs/table.bend: a table built from a list answers whatever the same descent over the list answers, so the three tables descend together and the question reduces to the three lists at a position.

laws.name: Inventory projection
laws.statement: Projection into source universe contains exactly the recorded source-domain OIDs, without assuming closure.
laws.proof_symbol: Inv.project_finds and Inv.project_only (proofs/inventory.bend), on Oid.eq_reflect, PSet.insert_keeps and PSet.insert_only
laws.backed_by: tools/differential.sh: inventory totals against `cat-file --batch-all-objects`, and no reported-missing object is actually present in the receiver.
laws.proved_part: Both directions. Every id on a receiver report that the source universe names has its ordinal in the projection, and the projection contains nothing but the ordinals the identity table returned for the reported ids. It rests on Oid.eq deciding equality of the complete digest -- no hash-collision assumption anywhere -- and on PSet.insert being pinned down at every ordinal.

C(A minus B) = C(A) minus C(B)

addressing_arithmetic.note: All five addressing facts are now proved: A1 (comparison agrees with the order), A2 (rebasing into a child), A3 (the tile address is injective), A4 (a leaf ordinal's word index is in range) and A5 (the walk agrees with the address), plus the converse range bound and what U32 addition computes.
addressing_arithmetic.A1: U32.cmp agrees with Nat.cmp on U32.to_nat. PROVED, as `comparing_two_ordinals_compares_their_values`. The power-of-two case was proved earlier for the set tree's descent; this is the general statement, and it is what the ascending-offsets invariant of a sparse leaf is stated with.
addressing_arithmetic.A2: U32.sub is subtraction when it does not borrow: from x < h+h and not x < h it follows that x-h < h. PROVED, as `rebasing_into_the_upper_half_keeps_the_ordinal_in_range`, together with A1 in the form that matters (`an_ordinal_is_below_a_power_of_two_exactly_when_it_fits_in_that_many_bits`). The half-width is always a power of two, which makes the whole question bitwise.
addressing_arithmetic.A3: PROVED, as `the_tile_address_is_injective`. The route is the division identity -- an ordinal is its word index scaled by 32 plus its bit index -- which turns equal addresses into equal `U32.to_nat`, and then `the_number_a_word_reads_as_determines_the_word` finishes. An earlier attempt stalled on word extensionality, whose natural statement takes a hypothesis quantified over bit positions that Bend's affine values will not let an induction use twice; the division identity avoids quantifying over bit positions entirely.
addressing_arithmetic.A4: x < 4096 implies x>>5 < 128. PROVED, as the chain `U32.hi_zero_shrn` plus `Word.to_nat_bound` in proofs/descend.bend, which is what lets the leaf laws discharge their width hypothesis.
addressing_arithmetic.proved: A bit index is below a word's width: Nat.gt(32, to_nat(and(x,31))). Discharged as `a_bit_index_is_below_the_word_width`.
addressing_arithmetic.A5: The walk and the tile address name the same positions. PROVED, as `the_walk_agrees_with_the_tile_address`.
addressing_arithmetic.converse: A number below 2^k fits in k bits (Word.to_nat_fits). Proved, so a range hypothesis can be derived from a numeric bound wherever a lemma needs the bitwise form.
